Photorealistic 35mm film still, same cinematography, colour grade, lighting and materials as the reference frame (warm tungsten work lamps, cream quilted padded fabric walls with metal ring frames, 1965 Soviet hardware, subtle film grain). NOT a drawing, NOT an illustration. Setting: the Volga inflatable airlock of Voskhod 2 at TRUE SCALE: a very narrow cylindrical tube only 1.0 metre in internal diameter and 2.5 m long, like a padded drainpipe. Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov in a bulky white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red straps and trim, white helmet with red CCCP lettering, backpack on his back. A graphite and coloured-pencil drawing on cream paper comes to life, still a pencil drawing in every frame: the same fine pencil lines, the same paper, the same drawing style as the first frame. The woman in the drawing sings the words 'bring me home' from the reference audio, her lips shaping each word in time with the voice: lips closing on 'b' and 'm', opening round and wide on 'home'. She sings with feeling: her brows and eyes respond to the music, her head tilts and lifts a little, she may close her eyes on a held note or glance up, her hair moves with her. Through all of it she stays the same person as in the first frame: the same large head, wide heart-shaped face with its tapering chin, high forehead, the two slightly different eyebrows, wide glasses, centre-parted hair, jacket and pink headphones on her head. Do not redraw, beautify, slim, age or restyle her face; no makeup, no added lines. Keep her high forehead exactly as drawn: the hairline and centre parting stay at the same height above her brows in every frame, never lowered, and the top of her head stays in frame. Static locked-off camera, no zoom or push-in: she stays framed chest-up exactly as in the first frame, never a face close-up. No text, no captions. She stands on a high platform above the clouds at night, under a sky full of white stars that stay in the sky the whole time. She wears loose, baggy dark cargo trousers, between navy blue and black, with a black belt and a long orange strap hanging down the front. As she sings she slowly lifts and spreads her arms wide, her face lifting a little to the sky; her hair and the open cropped jacket stir in the wind; the clouds drift slowly below. Her face is as expressive as a singer giving everything in a live performance: brows lifting and drawing together with the feeling of the words, eyes squeezing shut on the held note, mouth opening wide and round on 'home', cheeks lifting, her head moving with the phrase. Her whole body sings with her, not only her upper body: she shifts her weight from one foot to the other, her knees soften and bend a little as she breathes in, her hips sway, she rises slightly onto the balls of her feet as the note opens on 'home' and settles back, perhaps taking a small step forward. Steady camera, a slow gentle pull-back that keeps her in a medium shot, never tiny in the frame.

Photorealistic 35mm film still, NOT a drawing. Use the first reference image only for the cosmonaut's look: white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red harness straps, white helmet with red Cyrillic СССР, sweating red grimacing face with clenched teeth, film grade and grain. No flags or emblems. The Volga airlock interior (real 1965 design): the wall is pale off-white fabric bulging softly over about 40 inflated lengthwise ribs (air-filled booms) running the full length of the tube, like a ribbed sleeping bag; a thin maroon-brown foam padding collar only at the outer hatch rim; two small round lamps on the wall; a small grey duplicate control panel with a few toggle switches mounted on the wall near his hand. One end is a rigid metal ring with the round outer hatch, CLOSED; the other end is the capsule's round metal hatch. Inside diameter only 1.0 m, length 2.5 m; Leonov, 1.9 m long in his swollen suit, lies straight along it. Composition: a SIDE CUTAWAY. The sealed tube is shown cut open lengthwise like a cross-section diagram, but photographed for real, seen exactly from the side, filling the frame width; total darkness and black space all around it. The tube's length is 2.5 times its height. Inside, Leonov lies perfectly straight and horizontal along its full length, legs together, arms at his sides, boots pressed against the capsule-end hatch on the right, his helmet at the closed outer hatch on the left. The cut edge of the curved ribbed fabric wall arcs only a few inches above his helmet, chest and boots, and the bottom of the wall is right under him: he fills almost the whole height. The two small interior lamps give warm light inside, the only light in the image; the cut edge of the wall shows its double fabric layers and round inflated ribs in section. Straining, grimacing face in profile. 16:9. The second reference shows the real airlock's exterior construction.
